newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower, supplies seen plentiful.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower, supplies seen plentiful.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower, weakened by signs that charts are turning bearish and concern about a glut of supplies following a record crop in Kansas this year, dealers said.

They noted the market was struggling to absorb a Kansas wheat crop, estimated by the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service earlier this week at a record 492.2 million bushels, up from 255.2 million a year earlier.
"There is a little bit of demand around but nothing really exciting," one dealer said, noting supplies were plentiful with farmers starting to clear out bins ahead of fall harvest.
U.S. weekly net export sales of 641,700 tonnes, as reported by USDA, were slightly stronger than expected. Trade forecasts had ranged from 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Dealers also noted crop boosting rains in Australia and an improved planting outlook in Argentina were also among the current depressive factors.
Charts appeared to be turnish bearish with the market's five-week rally having possibly run its course.
September closed down 5-1/2 cents at $3.66-1/4 with other months down six cents to up 1-1/2 cents.
Prices have been edging higher since early July when the September contract set a contract low of $3.25.
Volume on wheat totalled 45.4 million bushels, up from 38.0 million on Wednesday.
